figures.shows: The finished Tetris in the Game view with its stats panel, the ghost piece, the preview of the next piece and the controls text
figures.caption: The finished game: the well in the middle, the score panel at the top left and the preview at the right.
figures.alt: A dark well ten cells wide with stacked colored cubes, a pale ghost piece under a falling piece, a panel with score, level and lines, and a small preview of the next piece.

figures.shows: The well from the front with the visible rows, the four hidden rows, the place where a piece appears and the preview panel's offset
figures.caption: Each cell stands at the world position of its column and row, and the hidden rows lie above the top row.
figures.alt: A tall rectangle of visible rows with a dashed strip of hidden rows above it, and arrows for columns and rows. A small square at the right is the rotation box of the next piece, with its bottom left cell at an offset of 12 columns and 15 rows.

figures.shows: The whole editor with Well and its five cubes in the Hierarchy and the empty well in the Game view
figures.caption: The Well entity groups the five cubes, and the Game view shows the well through the camera.
figures.alt: The editor window with the Hierarchy listing Well and the five cubes under it. The Game view shows a gray U of three cubes around a dark panel, with a smaller dark panel to its right.

figures.shows: The Console in play mode, its two Script lines new game with seed 60 and piece 1 is J, next I at the top, above the editor's lines
figures.caption: Read the two lines marked Script at the top: the script starts a game with the seed and logs its first two pieces. The lines below them are the editor's.
figures.alt: The Console panel. Its top two lines, marked Script, read Tetris: new game with seed 60 and Tetris: piece 1 is J, next I. Below them are three lines marked App, the editor's answers to the commands that started play, waited and showed the panel.

figures.shows: The Game view with the J piece at the top of the well, its ghost on the floor and the I piece in the preview
figures.caption: The first piece, its ghost and the next piece, drawn by cells that the script created.
figures.alt: A well with a blue piece near the top, a pale gray ghost of it on the floor and a light blue piece in the preview panel at the right.

figures.shows: The Game view in play with several locked pieces in the well, a piece falling and its ghost on the stack
figures.caption: The game can be played, and the ghost follows the falling piece.
figures.alt: A well with several colored pieces stacked at the bottom, a yellow square piece near the top and its pale gray ghost on the stack.

figures.shows: The Game view in play after one hard drop, with the score panel at the top left, the controls at the bottom left and the label above the preview
figures.caption: The score panel with its three texts at the top left, and the controls at the bottom left.
figures.alt: The Game view in play with a dark panel at the top left that reads Score: 36, Level: 1 and Lines: 0. Three lines of controls stand at the bottom left, and a label above the preview panel.

parameters.name: ControlsText
parameters.text:
Left/Right: move   Up/X, Z: rotate
Down: soft drop   Space: hard drop
P: pause   R: restart   Esc: quit

figures.shows: The whole editor beside a terminal that shows the play-test's log lines and the exit code 0
figures.caption: The play-test passes and the exit code is zero.
figures.alt: A terminal window with log lines about a cleared line and a game over, then a line that the command script finished, then the number 0.
figures.waitsFor: tier 3: a terminal beside the editor; the play-test runs from a terminal, and editor.screenshot shows only the editor's own window

figures.shows: The Console after the commands of the play-test file ran in an editor window on the project of stage 7: the game over with score 209, the new game after R, play stopped, two undo steps and the scene not modified
figures.caption: The play-test's commands run in an editor window, read in its Console. The Script line at 8.09 reports the game over: 14 pieces, score 209, lines 1 and level 2. The long App lines cut off at the right answer commands that set or read a value. An App line is logged when its command's answer arrives, so the new game that R starts shows before the key's line. Then play stops, two undo steps run, and the scene reports that it is not modified; no line reports a failed step.
figures.alt: The Console panel, each line with a time. Lines marked Script name pieces 5 to 13, then read Tetris: game over after 14 pieces; score 209, lines 1, level 2, and then a new game with seed 61. Lines marked App answer the commands after it: play stopped in the Edit state, two undo steps, and a scene report with modified false.
figures.numbers: 14 pieces, score 209, lines 1 and level 2 are read from the game-over line the script logs in the picture; the play-test's expectations check the same score, lines and level.
